target: tracker.sh supersede — the mid-stage gate applies here too, not only to shelve
cmd:
mkdir -p factory/specs; printf -- '---
id: 001
title: in-flight
status: building
---
body
' > factory/specs/001-a.md; printf -- '---
id: 002
title: reviewing-now
status: reviewing
---
body
' > factory/specs/002-b.md; printf -- '---
id: 003
title: at-rest
status: pr-open
---
body
' > factory/specs/003-c.md; source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh"; if tracker_supersede factory/specs/001-a.md me abc123 r >/dev/null 2>&1; then B=0; else B=$?; fi; if tracker_supersede factory/specs/002-b.md me abc123 r >/dev/null 2>&1; then R=0; else R=$?; fi; if TRACKER_FORCE_LIVE=1 tracker_supersede factory/specs/001-a.md me abc123 r >/dev/null 2>&1; then F=0; else F=$?; fi; if tracker_supersede factory/specs/003-c.md me abc123 r >/dev/null 2>&1; then A=0; else A=$?; fi; jq -n --argjson b "$B" --argjson r "$R" --argjson f "$F" --argjson a "$A" --arg s1 "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/001-a.md status)" --arg s2 "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/002-b.md status)" --arg s3 "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/003-c.md status)" --arg by2 "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/002-b.md superseded_by)" '{b: $b, r: $r, f: $f, a: $a, s1: $s1, s2: $s2, s3: $s3, by2: $by2}'
_note: shelve and supersede both take a spec out of the queue, so both can yank a file an unattended stage is mid-write on — but only shelve was gated, so a spec reading `building` could be superseded with no confirmation at all (found in the field on 2026-07-29, claude-deck spec 017). Guard B still prevented corruption, which is why this was a missing prompt rather than a data hole. Asserts all four arms: refused while building, refused while reviewing (writing nothing), forced through, and freely allowed at rest.
